summary: This is a plausible, self-gated primary. It halves each CTA's q-build, MMA tiles and gather bytes on the only sliding decode_1 kernel (10.8 us) and touches no other shape. Run it with the fixes listed: the reduce-scatter row mapping (HQ/C goes to 0), a C=16 occupancy >= 2 check, and making PERHEAD conditional on C=16 having routed. The headline will sit inside the CI, so read the result from the [slide-gate] PERHEAD-vs-C=16 line and the sliding decode_1 row, not from the geomean.
justification: Mechanism: at B=1 the sliding layer is one 16-CTA cluster on 132 SMs, so the shape's time is one CTA's latency chain. Each CTA gathers 128 old keys (one SK=128 sub-chunk, about 32 KB of K+V). Each warp builds 2 query heads (loop h = warp, warp+8, each with a cold qkv load, a shfl reduce and sincosf; at pos*fr <= 80000 rad sincosf stays on the fast Cody-Waite path, so the cost is the load more than the math). Each warp then attends 2 of the 8 tiles for its head. PERHEAD gives each warp 1 head and 1 tile and halves the gather to 4 x 16 B chunks per row. If the compiler does not hoist the second qkv load over the first iteration's smem store, the change also removes one serialised DRAM round trip per warp, which is the most likely source of a real gain (~0.5-1 us). The profile supports a latency-bound kernel: 10.8 us for 0.5 MB is about 48 GB/s, roughly 1.5% of HBM, and the floor is 0.1 us. The expectations are consistent with TASK.md: only the sliding decode_1 row (weight 46) moves. That is about 46 x 1.3 us = 60 us of the 1578 us decode_1 load, around 0.6% on the six-load geomean, well inside the [1.479, 1.530] CI. WEAKEST LINK: nothing shows that per-CTA work is a meaningful part of the 10.8 us. The chain is dominated by things PERHEAD does not shorten: dependent DRAM round trips (seq_lens -> page_table indices -> K/V gather), cluster launch and scheduling of a 16-wide non-portable cluster, two cluster.sync, and the DSMEM reduce. Halving the bytes per row does not halve the latency of one gather round trip. The 9.5 us target is optimistic, a 3% gate is plausible, and 'flat' is the most likely alternative. The gate makes a loss impossible by construction (master is kept), so a non-routing result is still informative if the gate line prints both times. Co-schedulability (extra note): the only measured occupancy in profiles shows cudaOccupancyMaxActiveClusters C=16 -> 14, so 2 clusters fit. The two clusters also have no cross-cluster dependency: disjoint output rows, disjoint 64-byte halves of the new cache row, no shared ticket, and the new k/v is read from smem, never from the cache. So serialisation could only slow it down, never deadlock or corrupt it, and the timing gate would catch the slowdown.
confounders: restack-sk-pseudo-cluster-plus-v3-fused-preattn (landed C=16 at B=1): this is the incumbent PERHEAD is gated against. The comparison is clean only if C=16 itself routed in the same process. If C=16 fell back to Triton (canary, self-check or its own timing gate), PERHEAD must stay off or must be gated against what is actually routed. As written ('vs master C=16') it can route against a C=16 that was never enabled.

restack-sliding-decode-sk-window-on-cluster-master (landed sk-window decode route): kernel_fn checks _sd_gate before _slide_gate. Today _SD_ROUTE only fills band 3 (B=17..32), so B=1 is not intercepted. The builder must keep that true; if band 1 can ever be filled, PERHEAD is dead code.
fused-preattention-triton / full-decode stream-K landings: no shared launch or memory traffic with the sliding B=1 single-node graph; no confound.

In-flight epilogue-gate-l2-prefetch-cuda (named by the hypothesis): it touches the CUDA epilogues, possibly including this kernel's gate read. If it lands first, the absolute times shift for both PERHEAD and C=16 alike; the interleaved gate ratio stays valid.
interference: No companion. The change is internally A/B'd: prepare times PERHEAD against master C=16 interleaved, with cold L2, the empty graph subtracted and the median of 31, and routes only at >= 1.03x. The printed gate line is therefore the attribution, independent of the headline. A scored companion could not resolve anything the gate line does not already resolve, and the headline delta (~0.6% expected) is below the CI either way. Requirement instead: the [slide-gate] PERHEAD line must print both times and the ratio whether or not it routes, and the profile's sliding decode_1 top kernel must show which template instance ran (e.g. by name or by the 32-CTA grid).
rules_flags: No rule problem in the design. It is graph-capturable, with a config-only branch (batch == 1 and PERHEAD route frozen at import), no host sync, no state derived from inputs, KV FP8, q E4M3 once, fp32 softmax and merges, bf16 out, and every window key attended by exactly one cluster per head.

The routing flag must be frozen at import or prepare, like _SLIDE_MOD, and must never be toggled per call in kernel_fn (standing policy against per-call mutable or global flag state). The provisional set/restore during _slide_route_checks is prepare-time only, as master already does.

Cluster-launch failure: slide_attn uses C10_CUDA_CHECK(cudaLaunchKernelEx), and kernel_fn may not try/except, so every failure mode has to be caught at prepare. The fixes are: (a) extend the occupancy test so PERHEAD requires occupancy_of(16) >= 2 (the current _SLIDE_NEED[16] = 1 only covers master's one cluster), else PERHEAD is off with the reason printed; (b) run the canary, self-check and two-state alternating replay through kernel_fn with the PERHEAD route provisionally set; (c) any exception there leaves master C=16 in place (not Triton, if C=16 had passed). Update slide_attn's TORCH_CHECK and grid to B * C * 2 for PERHEAD.

Reduce-scatter correctness: master uses NR = HQ / C rows per rank. With 8 rows per cluster and C = 16 that is 0, so nthr = 0 and no output is written. PERHEAD needs an explicit mapping: ranks 0..7 own one row each (16 threads x 4 dims, so the RMSNorm shfl stays in-warp) and ranks 8..15 skip, still joining both cluster.sync. Output row index = k*8 + row. The in-CTA staging merge must also loop over 8 slice warps per row, not over 4 warps x 2 heads.

Self-check: compare cache bytes per half. Each cluster's last rank writes only its 64 bytes, so the check must confirm that both halves of the new row are written (no stale half), on both kv_scale cases, and against master C=16's bytes.
open_questions: Does master's q-build loop issue its two qkv loads per warp back to back, or serialised behind the first iteration's smem store and sincosf? If they already overlap, the q-build half of the argument is mostly gone. SASS or a quick ncu source-level view of the existing C=16 kernel would settle it before the build.

Is the 10.8 us dominated by the seq_lens -> page_table -> gather dependency chain plus cluster launch? If so, a follow-up should attack that chain (for example, prefetching page indices for both clusters, or PDL from nothing). Neither more CTAs nor less work per CTA shortens it.

Do the two 16-CTA clusters land on separate GPCs, or do they share SMs (2 CTAs/SM at 101 KB smem)? If 32 CTAs pack onto 16 SMs, per-SM gather bandwidth and issue are shared and the halving partly cancels. Printing %smid or %clusterid once in the canary would show it.
Would C=8 per head (2 clusters x 8 CTAs = 16 CTAs, 256 keys each) be a cheaper variant to time in the same prepare gate? It needs no new occupancy assumption and keeps DSMEM fan-in at 8.
